record.original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A92 ([S-5]). Let a and m be positive integers. Then, in the ring Z[q], we have the following congruence 5am−1∑ k=0 q−2k(k+1) [2k k ] q F2k+1(q) ≡ 0 (mod [5 a]2 q).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an indeterminate $q$, define the $q$-integer $[n]_q = 1+q+q^2+\cdots+q^{n-1}$ for a positive integer $n$, the $q$-factorial $[n]_q! = [1]_q[2]_q\cdots[n]_q$ (with $[0]_q!=1$), and the Gaussian (q-binomial) coefficient
$$\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{k}_q = \frac{[n]_q!}{[k]_q!\,[n-k]_q!}.$$
Define the q-Fibonacci polynomials $F_n(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q]$ by
$$F_0(q)=0,\quad F_1(q)=1,\quad F_n(q)=F_{n-1}(q)+q^{\,n-2}F_{n-2}(q)\quad (n\ge 2).$$

Prove or disprove: for all positive integers $a$ and $m$, the following congruence holds in the Laurent polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}]$ (equivalently, after clearing the negative power, in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$):
$$\sum_{k=0}^{5^a m - 1} q^{-2k(k+1)} \genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{2k}{k}_q F_{2k+1}(q) \;\equiv\; 0 \pmod{[5^a]_q^{\,2}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of this specific q-congruence (often labeled Conjecture A92 in Z.-W. Sun's list of conjectures on q-Fibonacci/q-Lucas type sums modulo squares of cyclotomic-like factors $[5^a]_q^2$). Related work by Guo, Zudilin and others on q-supercongruences modulo cyclotomic polynomials exists, but no source explicitly confirms resolution of this statement, so its current status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: List of conjectures by Z.-W. Sun (Nanjing University)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive list of Sun's open conjectures, including q-analogue congruences involving q-Fibonacci numbers and q-binomial coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is collected among Sun's open conjectures and not marked as resolved.

status_evidence.title: A q-Microscope for Supercongruences (Guo–Zudilin)
status_evidence.snippet: Guo and Zudilin develop the 'creative microscoping' method for proving q-supercongruences modulo cyclotomic polynomials and their powers.
status_evidence.claim: Modern techniques exist for q-supercongruences mod $[n]_q^2$, but no proof of this particular q-Fibonacci sum identity is recorded.
